title: Iterative machine learning evolves DNA-nanotube sensors with higher dopamine selectivity
summary: A high-throughput platform synthesized 180 unique DNA-carbon nanotube sensors and tested 540 analyte/sensor conditions in under three days. An iterative machine learning pipeline predicted sequences for the next synthesis round, and dopamine sensitivity over interfering molecules such as ascorbic acid in complex media increased in up to 89% of the evolved sensors. The model type is not named in the abstract and an earlier arXiv version was not checked.
